raw_model_deviations.issue: The article presents a recipient’s belief that the call was AI and the subsequent discovery of a human as an actual event caused by the test. The ledger verifies that humans handled some calls, but not that a recipient experienced this reveal.
raw_model_deviations.explanation: The test involved human-handled calls, but the ledger does not report a recipient initially mistaking one for AI or experiencing a reveal; saying the test caused that exact surprise also asserts an unverified causal event.
raw_model_deviations.qualifier_text: A call seemed to come from an AI agent.
same_fact_id_locations: We Thought It Was AI—But There Was a Person Inside Meta’s Muse
It was like someone took off an AI costume. Then a person stepped out.
AI had not learned to speak like a human. A human stood behind the sign that said AI.
violation_spans: Ring, ring. A call seemed to come from an AI agent. But as the conversation went on, the voice was not AI at all. It was a person.
Meta had run a test that caused exactly this surprise.

raw_model_deviations.issue: The article describes the human role as taking over when AI finds a situation difficult. The ledger reports that trained contract workers made some calls instead of AI; it does not establish this fallback or handoff process.
raw_model_deviations.explanation: The claim adds a general AI-difficulty-to-human-handoff model beyond the ledger’s account of some calls being made and completed by human contract workers.
raw_model_deviations.qualifier_text: As a system, this may even be useful.
violation_spans: Having a person take over is not always a bad thing. A human can handle situations that AI alone finds difficult.
